choices.content:
Neither \((A)\) nor \((B)\) nor \((C)\) nor
\((D)\) is deducible from the given statements

question.prompt: Given the two hypotheses: I Some Mems are not Ens and II No Ens are Vees. If “some” means “at least one,” we can conclude that:

solutions.explanation:
A conclusion is deducible only if it holds in every arrangement satisfying both hypotheses. Hypothesis I guarantees a Mem outside the Ens. Hypothesis II restricts Ens, but says nothing about whether an object outside the Ens is a Vee.

First, suppose the only Mem and the only Vee are the same object \(u\), while the only En is a different object \(v\). Both hypotheses hold: \(u\) is a Mem that is not an En, and the En \(v\) is not a Vee. However, every Mem is a Vee and every Vee is a Mem. Thus A and B are false. C is also false because \(u\) is both a Mem and a Vee.

Next, suppose the only Mem is \(u\), the only En is \(v\), and the only Vee is \(w\), with all three objects distinct. Both hypotheses again hold, but no Mem is a Vee, so D is false.

Each of A through D fails in an arrangement allowed by the hypotheses. Therefore none is deducible, choice E.
solutions.title: Test the conclusions with examples
